freeze.definitions: ORB, FVG, IFVG, ICT-style sweep/shift/gap, head-and-shoulders neckline, and price-only liquidity sweep. All numeric parameters frozen before this study’s first performance run. User clarified IFVG and head-and-shoulders.
freeze.selection: 54 cells. Select using only Oct 22–Nov 6 development sessions; exclude incomplete Oct 30. Check on Nov 9–13 afterward. Nov 9–11 overlap earlier project research. Nov 12–13 are newly added, but the exercise remains retrospective, not a prospective trading trial.

research.title: FVG / IFVG geometry
research.finding: Platform education describes three-candle gaps and polarity inversions. These are pattern definitions, not evidence for a universal hit rate. Our entry and risk rules are specified research choices.

research.title: Liquidity sweep and ICT-style sequence
research.finding: Describes a sweep/reclaim and discusses structure-shift/FVG confirmation. ATAS is independent of ICT. Our price-only sequence omits discretionary bias, news and footprint analysis; it is not a complete replication of a named mentorship.

research.title: ICT origin reference
research.finding: The original 2022 Mentorship Episode 6 is provided as an origin reference. Only page metadata was accessible in this session; the full video was not reviewed. The executable subset is our disclosed hypothesis, not an assertion of reproducing the entire lesson.

research.title: Head-and-shoulders definition
research.finding: Broker education describes three peaks with a higher head, roughly level shoulders and completion on a neckline break. We add explicit pivot-confirmation and tolerance rules, and test fixed 2R rather than a chart-height target.

research.title: Opening range prior research
research.finding: A crude-oil-futures opening-breakout working-paper abstract reports results for its own threshold-based rule. It does not establish performance of our 15-minute MNQ opening-range rule.

research.title: Why selecting a best backtest can mislead
research.finding: Bailey and coauthors study backtest overfitting and selection among configurations. This lab does not calculate formal PBO or multiplicity-adjusted significance. Its development-only selection and later checks are safeguards, not proof of a durable edge.

limits: No perfect setup or guaranteed hit rate exists in these results. Qualified means the written conditions were satisfied before entry; it is not a probability of winning.
All 54 cells are experiments, not independent trades. Do not pool timeframes or windows into a portfolio: their trades may overlap and their rule lookbacks span different clock durations.

All directions are tested where the model permits them. Every variant uses the same 2R gross price target, $100 trade risk budget, $300 daily entry budget, maximum 3 MNQ, assumed $1.24 round-trip fee per contract and 1 adverse tick on entry/market or stop exits. Target touch assumes a fill without queue modeling.

Indicators and pivots use completed signal-chart bars only. Chart bars require contiguous source minutes. Entry is at the first contiguous minute open at confirmation; exits are resolved on the original one-minute bars. If stop and target touch together, stop wins. A position open at a minute’s start blocks a new entry at that minute, even if it later exits intrabar.

Entry windows are New York time: 09:45–11:30, 11:30–14:00 and 14:00–15:30. Positions may remain until 16:00. Rows are labeled by entry window, not exit time. ATR/state may use complete premarket chart bars from 07:00.
The opening range remains 09:30–09:44 in every ORB window. Only the first daily breakout attempt is eligible; late-window ORB cells may correctly have no observations.

Changing 1m/3m/5m changes the clock duration of bar-based gap expiry, sweep lookback, ATR and pivot confirmation. This is a disclosed joint model/timeframe comparison, not an isolated timeframe effect.
ICT is a broad framework. Sweep → shift → gap retest here is an analyst-defined price-only subset. A price sweep does not reveal resting orders, stop locations, or institutional intent.

Head-and-shoulders uses strict pivots confirmed two chart bars later; equality/outside-bar ambiguities are skipped. These extra tolerances and fixed 2R exits are research definitions, not universal pattern rules.

Yahoo MNQ=F is a vendor front-contract symbol without an exact contract identifier. Data checks do not certify exchange completeness or executable fills. No bid/ask series, latency/queue model, news calendar, margin or Topstep trailing-drawdown constraints are simulated.
Most cells have limited trades. Wilson 95% hit-rate intervals assume independent observations and are descriptive only; intraday dependence and selecting among 54 cells weaken inference.

Check-period results for all cells remain visible for audit, but looking for a new winner in those results would make them development data too. Only the preselected development choice has a selection-before-check interpretation.

Nov 9–11 were previously viewed in this project. Nov 12–13 are new to this study, not a live or genuinely prospective test. More untouched market history is needed before making an effectiveness claim.
Examples include winners and losers. Displayed setups are historical illustrations selected after outcomes, not evidence that a classifier could predict those outcomes.

models.name: ORB
models.rules: Freeze 09:30–09:44 New York. First chart close ≥ 1 point outside this range; one attempt per day, next-minute-open entry. Stop one chart ATR(14) from signal close. Later windows can have no trades because the first daily break has already happened.

models.name: FVG
models.rules: Three contiguous chart candles form a wick gap ≥ 1 point, with the middle body ≥ 0.5 ATR(14) in the gap direction. Within 10 chart bars, require a later touch and a directional candle closing beyond the gap midpoint. Stop beyond the far gap edge by 1 point. A close through that edge invalidates the original gap.

models.name: IFVG
models.rules: The same three-candle gap definition. Within 10 chart bars, a completed close through the opposite edge triggers inversion. Trade in the new direction, with the stop beyond the inversion candle and original gap by 1 point. This tests immediate close-confirmation, not a later inverse-gap retest.

models.name: ICT-style
models.rules: An analyst-defined subset, not all ICT teachings. Sweep and reclaim the previous 20 chart-bar high/low by ≥ 0.25 point. Within 5 bars, a directional candle with body ≥ ATR(14) must close through the opposite 5-bar structure level frozen before the sweep. A same-direction FVG then forms and is retested within 10 bars, with directional close beyond its midpoint. Stop beyond the sweep extreme by 1 point.

models.name: Head & shoulders
models.rules: Use alternating strict high/low pivots confirmed only after 2 bars on each side. Last 5 pivots must form H-L-H-L-H (or inverse), total span ≤ 40 bars, head ≥ 0.5 ATR beyond both shoulders and shoulders within 1 ATR. Project the neckline through the intervening pivots; require a completed close ≥ 0.25 point through it after right-shoulder confirmation. Stop beyond the right shoulder by 1 point. One attempt per pattern.

models.name: Liquidity sweep
models.rules: Price sweeps the previous 20 chart-bar high or low by ≥ 0.25 point and closes back inside the prior range. Enter next minute in the reclaim direction. A candle sweeping both sides is ambiguous and skipped. Stop beyond its extreme by 1 point. This is a price-only sweep proxy, not proof of stop orders or institutional intent.

selection.rule: At least 10 development trades; positive development net P&L and average realized R; positive development net under doubled costs. Rank by development average realized R, then net P&L, then ID. Never select using check-period results.
